title: Which Rule Wins?
look: Session board: two conflicting rule cards, the enforcement ladder, the scope ladder, the resolver's sorted list, rule packs and a session timeline on a dot-grid desk. Plain. Colors and type from the Zen-Sumi design system: washi paper, sumi ink, vermillion for mandatory, jade for the rule that holds. The Sensei mark on the close.

scenes.name: Two rules
scenes.desc: A dōjō rule and a repository rule disagree. Which one does the assistant follow?

scenes.name: Stronger first
scenes.desc: Mandatory, required, recommended, advisory: the stronger rule wins, and a mandatory rule is never overridden.

scenes.name: Then closer
scenes.desc: At equal strength the most specific scope wins: built-in, you, dōjō, workspace, repository.

scenes.name: Resolved
scenes.desc: Sensei gathers every rule, sorts by strength then scope, locks the mandatory ones, merges duplicates.

scenes.name: Rule packs
scenes.desc: Examples of rule sets: security, TDD, Clean Code, SOLID, compliance, UX, Ponytail, and stack packs adopted where the stack is found.

scenes.name: It sticks
scenes.desc: Mandatory and required rules are pushed at session start, re-sent at compaction, and a mandatory violation is blocked.

scenes.name: Sensei
scenes.desc: End card with the Sensei mark: the stronger rule wins, then the closer one.
